editorial_note: Scheduled cloud handoff-only run for 2026-10-02 (Friday). One real-estate/land-use story cleared the full primary-record + two-independent-origin + currency + image bar: Columbus has finalized the rezoning (Z26-022 / ordinance 2452-2026) of 21.3 acres at 600 Stimmel Road, including part of the city-owned McCoy Park, for a private NWSL training facility. No lifestyle story cleared the two-origin bar this run, so only one article was produced. The recurring Friday slot has no due format; the October 'What Rent Costs Here' (HUD FY2027 Fair Market Rents) format could not be produced because HUD's huduser.gov returned a 202 bot-challenge to every data-file and API request this run, and the recurring-format rule forbids estimating numbers, so it is held (see held_items). No import, image preparation, email delivery, or publication is claimed, and no git commit is treated as publication or downstream-import success.

story_facts_verified.project: Private National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) training facility proposed on 21.3 acres at 600 Stimmel Road, southwest Columbus, including part of the city-owned McCoy Park.
story_facts_verified.rezoning: Ordinance 2452-2026 / Rezoning case Z26-022: 600 Stimmel Rd. (43223), 21.3 acres, 310 feet east of Harmon Avenue (parcels 010-095231, 010-095234, 010-095233, 425-295576), from R-3/R/C-1/C-4 to CPD, Commercial Planned Development District (H-110). Proposed use: 'Private athletic training facility' described in the staff report as 'an athletic training facility for the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL).' Property owner: City of Columbus. Applicant: Phil Dangerfield c/o David Hodge, Atty.
story_facts_verified.legislative_timeline: Development Commission staff report dated August 13, 2026 with City Departments' recommendation of Conditional Approval pending a traffic access study; Southwest Area Commission recommendation for approval; ordinance introduced to council August 28, 2026; council Zoning Committee 'Approved' with the second reading waived at the September 14, 2026 Zoning Committee meeting (Legistar Event 6206, 6:30 PM, City Council Chambers Rm 231); signed by the council president September 14, by the mayor September 15, and attested by the city clerk September 16, 2026. Status 'Passed.' No individual roll-call tally is published in the Legistar record (motion by Rob Dorans, seconded by Nancy Day-Achauer, per the event item, but no vote count).
story_facts_verified.companion_park_funding: Ordinance 2204-2026 (Neighborhoods, Recreation & Parks Committee), passed September 16, 2026: authorizes modifying a Kimley-Horn and Associates contract for the 'Gender Road Park and McCoy Park Improvements Project' and the transfer/appropriation/expenditure of $941,941.53 from the Recreation and Parks Voted Bond Fund, with an emergency clause.
story_facts_verified.permit_check: City of Columbus Building Permits ArcGIS feature service (CC0), pulled 2026-10-02: a query for SITE_ADDRESS containing 'STIMMEL' returned zero permit records, consistent with a project that has cleared zoning but not filed for construction.
story_facts_verified.facility_specs_from_coverage: Independent coverage (WOSU June 9, 2026; NBC4/WCMH via Yahoo June 9, 2026; ABC6/WSYX April 24, 2026) describes a roughly $50 million Haslam Sports Group project: five soccer fields (three community, two full plus one partial for team practice), a two-story 45,000-square-foot training building with locker rooms and a cafeteria, heated grass fields, and about 200 parking spaces; $25M city + $25M county, $12M ownership contribution for food insecurity/early childhood, $3M toward new southwest-side parks; the original adaptive-park plan 'benched' after community opposition with a working group and replacement park pledged; groundbreaking targeted for later in 2026 and a 2028 inaugural season. These specs are attributed to the coverage, which predates and is broader (nearly 30 acres) than the 21.3-acre rezoning footprint.
story_facts_verified.geography: 600 Stimmel Rd geocoded 39.9353870,-83.0123746; McCoy Park 39.9368152,-83.0123329 (same location); Downtown Columbus 39.9602848,-83.0024576 (OpenStreetMap/Nominatim, ODbL, 2026-10-02).
story_facts_verified.original_contributions: Direct primary-record check of the Columbus Legistar legislative history (establishing that the rezoning is already final and enacted, correcting the pending-vote framing carried in prior briefs), the companion park-funding ordinance and its dollar figure, a building-permit dataset check showing no construction filing, a reconciliation of the 21.3-acre rezoning footprint against the ~30-acre figure in news coverage, and a CREN locator map.
story_facts_verified.limitations_stated: No individual roll-call vote tally is published; the facility's field count, building size, and acreage come from news coverage (April-June 2026) rather than the rezoning text; the ~30-acre figure in coverage is broader than the 21.3-acre rezoning footprint; the staff report's traffic access study condition and the separate replacement-park plan remain open.
